Marianne Kajbæk Vester-Andersen is a medical professional and clinical leader specializing in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in Denmark. She serves as a member of the steering committee for the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] (DANIBD), representing Region Zealand (Region Sjælland) [^src1]. Her professional titles include chief physician (ledende overlæge), PhD, and clinical lecturer (klinisk lektor) [^src1]. 

Her position on the DANIBD steering committee places her within the strategic leadership of a major national healthcare initiative. This broader effort aims to systematize and improve IBD treatment across Denmark through cross-regional quality measurement, standardized coding, and the evidence-based development of treatment guidelines. The steering committee oversees the evaluation of detailed quality data—such as the metrics collected between October 1, 2022, and September 30, 2023—which form the basis for clinical benchmarking, assessing treatment access, and identifying implementation challenges for specific quality indicators like patient education and the use of biologics or small molecules. Through her committee role, Vester-Andersen's work reflects a combination of clinical leadership, medical education, and quality measurement responsibilities within the Danish IBD framework [^src1].
